title: Anthropic offers Blackstone double-digit yield in latest chip financing
source_used: Reuters report on the Financial Times story (read at Devdiscourse and Global Banking & Finance Review)
key_facts: The Financial Times reported on Friday 16 Oct 2026, as relayed by Reuters, that Anthropic is offering Blackstone a yield of more than 10% to finance its latest chip deal.
Blackstone funds would invest $9 billion in the debt.
The debt is backed by Anthropic's five-year lease payments on the chips.
The FT cited people familiar with the matter.

Our 3 Oct 2026 edition: Bloomberg reported banks working with Broadcom were gathering $60 billion of financing for AI chips for Anthropic and others, with an $18 billion riskier slice led by Blackstone, which was committing $9 billion; the Reuters relay does not say whether this is the same deal.
quote_evidence: Anthropic is offering Blackstone a yield of more than 10% to finance its latest chip deal, the Financial Times reported on Friday.
Blackstone funds would invest $9 billion in the debt backed by Anthropic's five-year lease payments on the chips, the report said, citing people familiar with the matter.
why_it_matters_hint: A double-digit yield shows the price Anthropic is paying to borrow for computing hardware.
notes: FT original paywalled (HTTP 403 page with no text). Read Reuters' short relay. The GBF page adds an unsourced summary about an earlier $35 billion Apollo and Blackstone TPU package with yields of 5.75% and 8.5%; not used because it is not in Reuters' text. Link to the 3 Oct deal comes from our own 3 Oct edition and is not confirmed by the FT relay.
